25786-american-sketches.title: American Sketches
25786-american-sketches.creator: Charles Whibley
25786-american-sketches.description: A book by Charles Whibley. , so New York is not a city--it is a collection of cities. Here, on the narrow rock which sustains the real metropolis of the United States, is room or men and women of every faith and every race. The advertisements which glitter in the windows or are plastered upon the hoardings suggest that all nationalities meet with an equal and a flattering acceptance.

39549-the-carved-lions.title: The Carved Lions
39549-the-carved-lions.creator: Mrs. Molesworth
39549-the-carved-lions.description: A book by Mrs. Molesworth. I can remember things in my little girlhood more clearly than many in later years. This makes me hope that the story of some part of it may interest children of to-day, for I know I have not forgotten the feelings I had as a child.

arxiv-2105-06576.title: Z Z -Boson Decays into Majorana or Dirac (Heavy) Neutrinos
arxiv-2105-06576.creator: Alain Blondel, André de Gouvêa, Boris Kayser
arxiv-2105-06576.description: Abstract We computed the kinematics of Z Z -boson decay into a heavy–light neutrino pair when the Z Z -boson is produced at rest in e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collisions, including the subsequent decay of the heavy neutrino into a visible final state containing a charged-lepton.

arxiv-2106-04814.title: Making Better Use of Bilingual Information for Cross-Lingual AMR Parsing
arxiv-2106-04814.creator: Yitao Cai, Zhe Lin, Xiaojun Wan
arxiv-2106-04814.description: Abstract Abstract Meaning Representation (AMR) is a rooted, labeled, acyclic graph representing the semantics of natural language. As previous works show, although AMR is designed for English at first, it can also represent semantics in other languages. However, they find that concepts in their predicted AMR graphs are less specific.

arxiv-2206-11990.title: Equiformer: Equivariant Graph Attention Transformer for 3D Atomistic Graphs
arxiv-2206-11990.creator: Yi-Lun Liao, Tess Smidt
arxiv-2206-11990.description: Abstract Despite their widespread success in various domains, Transformer networks have yet to perform well across datasets in the domain of 3D atomistic graphs such as molecules even when 3D-related inductive biases like translational invariance and rotational equivariance are considered.

arxiv-2208-13415.title: Cooperative coevolutionary hybrid NSGA-II with Linkage Measurement Minimization for Large-scale Multi-objective optimization
arxiv-2208-13415.creator: Rui Zhong, Masaharu Munetomo
arxiv-2208-13415.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a variable grouping method based on cooperative coevolution for large-scale multi-objective problems (LSMOPs), named Linkage Measurement Minimization (LMM). And for the sub-problem optimization stage, a hybrid NSGA-II with a Gaussian sampling operator based on an estimated convergence point is proposed.

arxiv-2404-18687.title: Socially Adaptive Path Planning Based on Generative Adversarial Network
arxiv-2404-18687.creator: Yao Wang, Yuqi Kong, Wenzheng Chi*, Lining Sun
arxiv-2404-18687.description: Abstract Note to Practitioners The motivation of this work is to provide an efficient learning-based method to guide the robot generate the path in human-robot interaction environments. Conventional path planning algorithms can quickly generate the optimal path from the start to the goal.

arxiv-2411-10656.title: Precision or Peril: A PoC of Python Code Quality from Quantized Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-10656.creator: Eric L. Melin, Adam J. Torek, Nasir U. Eisty, Casey Kennington
arxiv-2411-10656.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Eric L. Melin, Adam J. Torek, Nasir U. Eisty, Casey Kennington. Context: Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-5 and LLaMA-405b exhibit advanced code generation abilities, but their deployment demands substantial computation resources and energy. Quantization can reduce memory footprint and hardware requirements, yet may degrade code quality. Objective: This study investigates code generation performance of smaller LLMs, examines the effect of quantization, and identifies common code quality issues as a proof of concepts (PoC).

arxiv-2412-13463.title: FlexPose: Pose Distribution Adaptation with Limited Guidance
arxiv-2412-13463.creator: Zixiao Wang Junwu Weng Mengyuan Liu Bei Yu
arxiv-2412-13463.description: Abstract Numerous well-annotated human key-point datasets are publicly available to date. However, annotating human poses for newly collected images is still a costly and time-consuming progress. Pose distributions from different datasets share similar pose hinge-structure priors with different geometric transformations, such as pivot orientation, joint rotation, and bone length ratio.

arxiv-2501-12230.title: Cold gas bubble inflated by a low-luminosity radio jet
arxiv-2501-12230.creator: Suma Murthy, Raffaella Morganti, Tom Oosterloo, Dipanjan Mukherjee, Suude Bayram, Pierre Guillard, Alexander Y. Wagner, Geoffrey Bicknell
arxiv-2501-12230.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Suma Murthy, Raffaella Morganti, Tom Oosterloo, Dipanjan Mukherjee, Suude Bayram, Pierre Guillard, Alexander Y. Wagner, Geoffrey Bicknell. We present NOEMA CO(2-1) observations of a nearby, young, low-luminosity radio source, B2 0258+35. Our earlier CO(1-0) study had shown the presence of strong jet-ISM interaction and a massive molecular gas outflow involving 75% of the circumnuclear gas.

arxiv-2505-20451.title: Amulet : Putting Complex Multi-Turn Conversations on the Stand with LLM Juries
arxiv-2505-20451.creator: Sahana Ramnath, Anurag Mudgil, Brihi Joshi, Skyler Hallinan, Xiang Ren
arxiv-2505-20451.description: Abstract Today, large language models are widely used as judges to evaluate responses from other language models. Hence, it is imperative to benchmark and improve these LLM-judges on real-world language model usage: a typical human-assistant conversation is lengthy, and shows significant diversity in topics, intents, and requirements across turns, e.g. social interactions, task requests, feedback.

arxiv-2602-20789.title: Photosynthetic exergy I. Thermodynamic limits for habitable-zone planets 2026 Photosynthetic exergy I. Thermodynamic limits for habitable-zone planets – C
arxiv-2602-20789.creator: Giovanni Covone, Amedeo Balbi
arxiv-2602-20789.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Covone, Amedeo Balbi. Photosynthesis is central to Earth’s biosphere and a prime candidate for sustaining complex life on habitable exoplanets, yet a thermodynamically consistent treatment of the work potential of stellar radiation at planetary surfaces is still lacking. We develop a radiative–thermodynamic framework that quantifies the maximum useful work (exergy) extractable for a given star–planet configuration and yields exergy-based bounds on photosynthetic power and long-wavelength absorption cutoffs.

pmc-10607146.title: Niche and Range Shifts of Aedes aegypti and Ae. albopictus Suggest That the Latecomer Shows a Greater Invasiveness
pmc-10607146.creator: Peixiao Nie, Jianmeng Feng, Bernard D Roitberg
pmc-10607146.description: Simple SummaryAs the two major vectors of mosquito-borne pathogens, yellow fever (Aedes aegypti) and Asian tiger (Ae. albopictus) mosquitos are greatly threatening human health globally. However, their niche and range shifts remain little known. Using the largest occurrence record datasets to date, the present study examined the niche and range shifts between the native and invasive Ae. aegypti and Ae.

pmc-10740764.title: Diet and Aging: The Role of Polyphenol-Rich Diets in Slow Down the Shortening of Telomeres: A Review
pmc-10740764.creator: Stefania D’Angelo, Adrianne Bendich
pmc-10740764.description: The ends of human chromosomes are defended by DNA–protein complexes named telomeres, which inhibit the chromosomes from fusing with each other and from being known as a double-strand break by DNA reparation proteins. Telomere length is a marker of biological aging, and disfunction of telomeres is related to age-related syndromes.

pmc-12721051.title: Unveiling the influence of temperature treatments on the structural and Metabolomic profile of Pandan leaves (Pandanus amaryllifolius) instant powder: a multi-analysis approach
pmc-12721051.creator: Chengxu Liu, Zhen Zhang, Yuqi Xin, Yuanyuan Zhang, Yiyun Wu, Chuanrui Luo, Peishi Liu, Yewei Huang, Cunchao Zhao, Ya Wang
pmc-12721051.description: Pandan leaves (Pandanus amaryllifolius), widely used in Southeast Asia, hold significant promise for natural product and fragrance industries, though underutilized due to limited processing technologies. This study investigated the impact of three temperature-based extraction methods—room temperature (RT), low temperature (LT), and high temperature (HT) on the structural and flavor properties of instant pandan leaf powder.

pmc-12729165.title: Isolation of enzyme-producing microbial strains and their effects on the color and quality of tobacco stems
pmc-12729165.creator: Honglin Zhang, Jinghua Zhang, Tingju Liu, Jinhui Jiang, Chaojun Shi, Ze Liu, Lương Hùng Tiến, Hoàng Trung Tín, Jindan Wang, Neng Yang, Yinbiao Zhou, Ruilin Fu, Jiahao Jia, Yumei Dong, Jun Li, Tao Liu
pmc-12729165.description: China is one of the world’s major tobacco producers, yielding more than 2.2 million tons of tobacco leaves annually, among which approximately 25–30% constitute by-products such as tobacco stems. Dark-colored stems are favored for their high contents of reducing and total sugars, porous structure, thermal stability, and rich aroma precursors; however, their limited availability constrains large-scale industrial utilization.

pmc-13181393.creator: Wei Sun, Yu Lu, Zhenghong Cao, Cuiping Xin, Kexin Fan, Xiangchao Kong, Xiaolong Chen, Mingyu Zhang, Qi-Jun Chen
pmc-13181393.description: An uncleavable fusion of prime editors with the Csy4 CRISPR RNA endonuclease efficiently generates heritable mutations in Arabidopsis with reduced Csy4-associated toxicity. pmc-13219087.title: Mitochondrial super complexes in the colorless chlorophycean alga Polytomella parva
pmc-13219087.creator: Marcos Ostolga-Chavarría, Anaiza Rico-Luna, Sergio Fuentes-Hernández, Héctor V. Miranda-Astudillo, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, Diego González-Halphen
pmc-13219087.description: Chlorophycean algae of the genera Chlamydomonas and Polytomella share a common photosynthetic ancestor. However, members of the Polytomella lineage have adopted a heterotrophic lifestyle, having lost the photosynthetic apparatus and relying instead on acetate or ethanol as carbon sources, with energy production centered on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS).

pmc-13238161.description: Objective:To investigate the value of nucleic acid testing (NAT) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in the screening of Hepatitis-B virus (HBV) in blood samples from voluntary blood donors.Methodology:This was a retrospective observational study. Five hundred blood samples from healthy blood donors collected by the Baoding No.

pmc-13348859.title: Comparing geriatric assessment tools for predicting negative health outcomes in older adults
pmc-13348859.creator: Ahmad Abbadi, Francesco Innocenti, Giorgi Beridze, Emmanouil Kokoroskos, Alberto Zucchelli, Tobias Nordström, Caroline Wachtler, Laura Fratiglioni, Davide L Vetrano, Amaia Calderón-Larrañaga
pmc-13348859.description: BackgroundAmid global population aging, evidence-based geriatric assessment tools are essential for clinical decision-making and risk stratification. Despite growing interest, few studies have comprehensively compared the discriminative ability of existing tools, particularly as new tools have recently become available. In this study, we aimed to perform such a comparison across a wide range of patient-relevant health outcomes.

pmc-13380363.title: Response to letter: ‘Towards equitable implementation of AI‐assisted screening for diabetic retinopathy: Perspectives on digital literacy, trust and system readiness in developing countries’
pmc-13380363.creator: Umar A. R. Chaudhry, Lakshmi Chandrasekaran, Alicja R. Rudnicka, On Behalf the ARIAS Research Group
pmc-13380363.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). s as follows: This study 1 was conducted in England, and respondents were from socio‐demographic population groups across different ages, sexes and ethnicities. We acknowledge that there are differences in perspectives for people living with diabetes and healthcare professionals based in different countries, particularly those from low‐ and middle‐income countries, and the study findings may not necessarily translate outside of the English NHS landscape.

pmc-13677999.title: Application of CAR-T cell therapy in orthopedics: From bone malignancies to non-malignant musculoskeletal disorders
pmc-13677999.creator: Yimei Que, Xienilai Xie, Wei Xie, Yunzhou Zuo, Wang Chen, Zedong Xu, Changtian Gong, Xugui Li
pmc-13677999.description: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed hematologic oncology, but its application in orthopaedic diseases remains at an early stage. In bone malignancies, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and bone metastases, antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, and the immunosuppressive skeletal microenvironment restrict efficacy.
